title: Lesson 50: Privacy: PII, Data Minimization, Retention, and Consent for AI
description: The privacy layer that decides what may be processed about a person at all: recognizing PII and special categories, keeping the least data for the shortest time, and honoring real, demonstrable, withdrawable consent.

questions.question: Why is a customer ID on its own still treated as personal data in an agent pipeline?
options: Because any identifier that can point to a person counts as personal data
Because customer IDs always contain a name embedded somewhere in the string
Because only data that names a person explicitly is considered regulated
Because IDs are treated as personal data only once they are stored
questions.explanation: Personal data covers anything that can identify a person directly or in combination with other information, so recognition must span the assembled context rather than only obvious fields like a name.

questions.question: Where does data minimization have to live for it to actually work?
options: In a system prompt that asks the model to use only necessary data
In a review meeting held after the agent has already shipped
In the architecture, in what the pipeline fetches and passes
In the model's training data, which filters out excess fields
questions.explanation: A prompt instruction is a request the model may ignore, so over-collection happens before the model is even called. Minimization is a control you build into retrieval, the tool interface, and input transformation.

questions.question: Why does retention for an agent have to be applied per store rather than once?
options: Because each store has a different legal jurisdiction
Because the data becomes many separate copies of the same record
Because databases cannot run scheduled deletions
Because the model refuses to delete any of its own cached context
questions.explanation: The prompt, retrieved context, trace, embeddings, and logs are each separate copies of the same personal data. Removing only the source record leaves the person's data retained elsewhere, so each store needs its own expiration.
